A development method for hardware and software

SimulationDrivenDevelopment

Define done as a measurable outcome in a simulated world.

Iterate until the simulation gets there.

Keep the simulation honest with real measurements.

A term and method by Chad Cox. Draft 0, November 2026.

Contrast

A test checks the code. A simulation checks the outcome.

Test driven

Is the code correct?

The answer is pass or fail.

assert cart.total() == 42.00

Simulation driven

Does the thing work in its world?

The answer is a score against a threshold.

Hardware: 95 of 100 simulated runs clear a 7.5 inch step carrying 20 lbs.

Software: 80% of first-time visitors finish setup in under 3 minutes.

You keep your tests. SDD adds a referee for the question tests cannot answer.

The loop

Five steps. Three of them repeat.

  1. Step 1

    Specify

    Write done as a number: an outcome, a threshold, and how many runs.

  2. Step 2

    Simulate

    Run the design in a simulated world. Physics for hardware, simulated users for software.

  3. Step 3

    Score

    Measure the runs against the threshold, and report the noise.

  4. Step 4

    Revise

    Change the design. Leave the spec and the simulation alone.

  5. Step 5

    Calibrate

    Measure the real thing. Where the simulation predicted wrong, fix the simulation.

Steps 2 to 4 repeat until the threshold holds. They can run unattended. The simulation supplies the feedback a person would otherwise give, so a coding agent can work toward the goal on its own.

Rules

Five rules that keep it from becoming a video game.

Done is a number.
If you cannot measure it, you cannot simulate toward it.
The builder never touches the referee.
Whoever revises the work, person or agent, cannot edit the spec, the simulated world, or the scorer.
Trust is earned by prediction.
A simulation is believed once it predicts something you already measured. Calibrate first, and publish the gap.
Report the noise.
Simulations are statistical. A difference inside the noise is not a result.
Hold something back.
Keep scenarios the builder never sees. They catch a design that learned to please the simulation and nothing else.

Simulators

One method, two simulators.

Hardware

Simulated by
A physics engine running the machine through its task, many times.
Calibrated by
Bench measurements of the real machine: weights, torques, timings.

Software

Simulated by
Simulated users with human limits. They skim, lose patience, mis-tap, and quit.
Calibrated by
Real analytics and real people doing the same task.

Physics is the stricter referee. Simulated users lean agreeable and efficient, so they need calibration the most.

Lineage

What it builds on.

  • Test driven development. Write the check first, then make it pass.
  • Simulation-driven design in mechanical engineering. Run structural and fluid analysis early, so the analysis shapes the design.
  • Deterministic simulation testing at FoundationDB, TigerBeetle, and Antithesis. Run a whole system inside a simulated world of failures.
  • Simulated users. UXAgent and AgentA/B send LLM agents with personas through real websites.

What SDD adds: the simulation as the definition of done, a loop that revises until the threshold holds, and calibration as a required step.
